correctness.rationale: The support formula is a maximum of orthogonal disk support functions. The m=2 CDF follows from a two-boundary spherical probability derivative and has been independently compared to conditional quadrature. The second moment is a direct rotational identity. The lower-edge coefficient is computed from a Dirichlet(1/2) density integrated over the exact transverse simplex with uniform error control; the upper-edge uses beta marginal laws and pair-overlap estimates. The high-dimensional mixed law follows from a Gaussian extreme-value limit with independent Z0^2 and a vanishing denominator effect. All checker families run successfully; they are diagnostics and not replacements for these analytic steps.

originality.rationale: The exact same centered two-disk geometry and its deterministic support/mean are expressly credited to Finch (2012). A relevant complete published three-hyperdisk width theorem and a two-disk separation mean-width theorem were inspected; neither covers the shared-axis maximum-plus-coordinate width distribution, the m-dimensional endpoint laws or the independent Gumbel-plus-half-chi-square limit. Public literature searches found no direct combined theorem. This remains a same-model priority judgment, with nonzero risk of an unindexed Dirichlet order-statistic formula.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently titled Dirichlet(1/2) maximum / spherical-coordinate distribution may contain a mathematically equivalent width law.
The all-dimensional model can be described as a coordinate-subspace atomic norm; other norm-literature formulations may reproduce some constants.
Bäsel arXiv:1604.07245 was screened by abstract, not full text; it concerns the separated oloid rather than the centered or high-dimensional model.
Originality has not been independently audited.

value.rationale: The complete directional-width law of the classical centered orthogonal-disk hull is a natural exact invariant beyond Finch’s established mean. The all-dimensional common-axis geometry has a sharp isolated-minimum versus circle-maximum stratification, producing two distinct explicit powers. Its mixed Gumbel-plus-half-chi-square weak limit reveals a genuine surviving shared-axis Gaussian contribution that is absent from the published coordinate-hyperdisk model. These form a motivated complete finite-dimensional special classification plus general geometric endpoint and limit laws, not a routine parameter increment.
